title: Motion Design Producer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI’s in-house Creative Team is looking for a Motion Design Producer to help shape and scale how our brand comes to life through motion design across every touchpoint — from identity systems and campaigns to product, web, and comms work.

You’ll partner closely with our Brand Identity & Brand Design leadership to manage intake, resourcing, timelines, and creative workflows — ensuring design projects move seamlessly from concept to delivery. You’ll serve as the operational backbone of the design practice, building clarity and momentum across a growing cross-functional team. As Motion Design is a shared function in Creative Design, you will also partner closely with other production functional ecosystems to deliver motion design support.

This is a highly collaborative role that requires both strategic oversight and hands-on execution. You’ll be a key connector across Marketing, Product, Comms, and Web — driving alignment, enabling great design, and creating the systems that keep our creative work consistent, efficient, and impactful.

In this role, you will:

  • Manage Day-to-day Motion Design Operations: Oversee the end-to-end management of design projects — from scoping and prioritization to delivery — ensuring resources, timelines, and dependencies are well-planned and communicated.

  • Produce High-Priority Motion Projects: Serve as a hands-on individual contributor (IC) on large, high-priority motion projects, owning production from kickoff through delivery.

  • Shape Intake & Resourcing: Partner with creative and marketing, creative, production and ops leads to evaluate new requests, define scope, and allocate design capacity across internal and external partners.

  • Build Cross-Functional Alignment: Act as the connective tissue between design and partner teams (Product, Web, Brand, Comms, and GTM), ensuring design work ladders up to broader strategic goals.

  • Elevate Systems & Process: Design and implement operational frameworks that enable the design team to scale effectively — from creative reviews and feedback loops to asset tracking and tool optimization.

  • Manage External Partners: Oversee relationships with design vendors, freelancers, and production partners; ensure output meets OpenAI’s creative and technical standards.

  • Uphold Craft & Consistency: Partner with the Brand Identity and Brand Design team to ensure design work is cohesive, high-quality, and reflective of OpenAI’s evolving visual identity.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 8+ years of experience in design production, brand operations, or creative program management within an in-house team or agency environment.

  • Are fluent in the design process — from concept and iteration through production and delivery — and can anticipate what a creative team needs to succeed. Should be experienced in full identity explorations and production needs.

  • Are a natural systems-builder who can bring order to complexity without stifling creativity.

  • Excel at stakeholder management and communication — you’re equally comfortable talking to designers, executives, and engineers.

  • Are proactive, unflappable, and skilled at driving clarity in fast-moving environments.

  • Are fluent in tools like Asana, Airtable, Figma, and Google Workspace.

  • Have experience building or scaling global brand systems.

  • Have familiarity with motion, 3D, or experiential design production.

  • Have a strong understanding of creative operations in a technology-driven or design-led organization.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Motion Designer to help tell the stories behind our research. You’ll translate complex ideas, emerging capabilities, and the work of our researchers into clear, engaging motion across films, launches, demos, and other communications.

Working within the creative team, you’ll partner with Research, Brand, and production teams to shape work from early concepts through final delivery. You’ll explore visual approaches, develop original design and animation, and help bring other artists’ contributions together into a cohesive result.

This is a hands-on role for someone with strong motion craft, curiosity about unfamiliar subjects, and confidence working with open-ended briefs. Alongside your own execution, you’ll provide feedback to fellow artists, help establish creative standards, and take ownership of motion quality across assigned projects.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop motion concepts for research stories, working with creative partners and subject matter experts to make complex ideas visually clear while preserving their underlying meaning.

  • Design and produce high-quality 2D and 3D motion for research films, launches, demos, and supporting content, from storyboards and animatics through final delivery.

  • Apply compositing and VFX expertise to develop and execute complex visual sequences.

  • Apply and extend OpenAI’s visual and motion language, balancing consistency with the needs of each story.

  • Take ownership of motion quality across assigned projects, bringing individual contributions together into a cohesive result. Help establish and maintain shared standards for craft and visual consistency through project reviews, references, and practical guidance.

  • Provide actionable creative and technical feedback, mentor fellow artists to strengthen their craft, and share techniques while remaining hands-on.

  • Collaborate closely with designers, filmmakers, editors, producers, and researchers to shape work from early concepts through final delivery.

  • Work with producers to scope projects, communicate dependencies, and maintain a high standard of craft as priorities and timelines evolve.

  • Present work clearly, explain creative decisions, and incorporate feedback from creative and technical partners.

  • Develop reusable assets, templates, and workflows where they improve quality and make recurring work easier to produce.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 7+ years of experience in motion design across films, campaigns, launches, or other narrative work.

  • A strong portfolio demonstrating design judgment, animation craft, and the ability to carry an idea from concept through finished execution.

  • The ability to explore an open-ended brief, develop a clear visual approach, and refine it through collaboration.

  • Experience providing constructive feedback to other artists and bringing multiple contributors’ work together into a cohesive result.

  • Proficiency in After Effects and experience with Cinema 4D or comparable 3D tools, alongside editing and compositing workflows.

  • Comfort working in Figma and sharing work across design and production teams.

  • A strong understanding of typography, composition, timing, rhythm, and visual storytelling.

  • Experience making complex or unfamiliar subjects understandable through design and motion.

  • Experience working with subject matter experts and incorporating technical feedback without losing clarity or creative quality.

  • Curiosity about AI and research, and a willingness to learn enough about a subject to represent it thoughtfully.

title: Video Strategist
region: San Francisco, CA • New York, NY • United States
description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

Video is one of the most powerful ways we bring the Figma brand to life, and we are building the function to match that ambition. As a Video Strategist, you will define what video does for this brand and build the operation that delivers it: the strategy, the franchises people come back for, the production model behind them, and eventually the team that runs it all. You will sit within Brand Marketing and partner closely with design, creative, comms, product marketing, community, and advocacy to turn complex product and customer stories into work people want to watch and share.

This is a rare combination. Figma is a beloved brand with a creative community that already wants to hear from us, and a video function that is still yours to build.

This is a full time role based in San Francisco or New York hub, or remotely in the United States.

What you’ll do at Figma:

  • Set the strategy: Define the role video plays across brand, social, editorial, product launch, community, and event moments. Own the format architecture and the prioritization framework that decides what we make and what we pass on
  • Build franchises: Create and run a portfolio of recurring video programs that compound audience over time, alongside the campaign and launch work. Own the development pipeline for new formats and the call to renew, evolve, or retire a series
  • Build the engine: Decide what we produce in-house, what goes to agencies and directors, and what we source from creators, with the economics behind each. Own the video budget and vendor relationships, and build the standards we are missing today around briefing, review, rights, and asset reuse
  • Lead the craft: Set and hold the quality bar for video made anywhere under the Figma brand. Write and approve briefs, run creative reviews, and enable cross-functional teams producing their own video with guardrails and coaching rather than gatekeeping
  • Measure what matters: Partner with our Brand Marketing Technologist to define what good looks like for each format and franchise, instrument it, and report it in a way that changes what we make next
  • Grow the team: Lead, hire, and develop the video team and the external bench, and make the case for the resourcing the strategy requires

We'd love to hear from you if you have:

  • 10+ years across video, brand storytelling, editorial, content strategy, or production leadership, including several years leading a video function or team
  • A track record creating and running recurring video franchises that outlasted a single season and grew an audience
  • Experience owning a production model end to end: the in-house versus agency versus creator call, a real budget, and the partner relationships behind it
  • People leadership. You have hired, developed, and given hard feedback to producers, editors, or an external bench
  • Fluency across the format spectrum, from social-first short-form to long-form storytelling, launch films, and customer narratives, with clear opinions on what each format is good for
  • The ability to set a creative bar for work made by people who do not report to you, and to hold it without becoming the bottleneck
  • Comfort as the video voice in rooms with senior stakeholders, including the judgment to disagree productively and the measurement literacy to defend your decisions

While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • Hands-on editing or motion graphics ability. We are not hiring you to sit on a timeline, but craft fluency sharpens judgment and helps you move fast
  • Experience with live event and conference content at scale
  • Familiarity with music licensing, talent releases, and usage rights at volume
  • Experience building creator and influencer partnerships
  • Experience scaling video inside a company going through rapid growth or a brand evolution
At Figma, one of our values is Grow as you go. We believe in hiring smart, curious people who are excited to learn and develop their skills. If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with the points outlined in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Pay Transparency Disclosure

Job level and actual compensation will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process (including skills and prior relevant experience, potential impact, and scope of role), market demands, and specific work location.

Figma offers equity to employees, as well as a competitive package of additional benefits, including health, dental, and vision coverage; retirement benefits with company contributions; parental leave and reproductive or family planning support; mental health and wellness benefits; and paid time off. Figma provides paid sick leave, holidays, and other leave benefits in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the requirements of the Washington Minimum Wage Act and related regulations. Exempt employees are eligible for employer‑provided paid flexible PTO in addition to flexible paid sick leave. PTO is subject to manager approval. Additional benefits may include company recharge days, cell phone and home internet reimbursements, and a number of lifestyle spending accounts. Figma also offers sales incentive compensation for most sales roles and an annual bonus plan for eligible non-sales roles. All compensation and benefits are subject to applicable plan terms and may be modified by Figma at any time, consistent with applicable law.

Annual Base Salary Range:
$153,000—$269,000 USD

At Figma we celebrate and support our differences. We know employing a team rich in diverse thoughts, experiences, and opinions allows our employees, our product and our community to flourish. Figma is an equal opportunity workplace - we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity/expression, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to apply for a role, participate in the interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. If you require accommodation, please reach out to accommodations-ext@figma.com. These modifications enable an individual with a disability to have an equal opportunity not only to get a job, but successfully perform their job tasks to the same extent as people without disabilities.

Examples of accommodations include but are not limited to:

  • Holding interviews in an accessible location
  • Enabling closed captioning on video conferencing
  • Ensuring all written communication be compatible with screen readers
  • Changing the mode or format of interviews

To ensure the integrity of our hiring process and facilitate a more personal connection, we require all candidates keep their cameras on during video interviews. Additionally, if hired you will be required to attend in person onboarding.

By applying for this job, the candidate acknowledges and agrees that any personal data contained in their application or supporting materials will be processed in accordance with Figma's Candidate Privacy Notice.

Application limits: To help candidates focus on the opportunities most relevant to their skills and experience, Figma limits the number and frequency of applications. These limits apply to all roles:

  • Candidates may submit up to 5 applications during any rolling 30-day period.
  • Candidates may not reapply to the same role while an application is active or within 90 days of receiving a rejection.

Once the applicable days has passed, candidates are welcome to apply again.

title: Motion Designer + Editor, Social
description:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.

About the role

*Open to hiring remote across North America. We have offices in NYC, San Francisco, and Seattle.

We’re looking for an AI-Native Social Media Creative, a creative generalist who works natively with AI tools to produce exceptional short-form work for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and X. Your background might be in editing, directing, design, animation, art direction or writing. What matters is that you’re already deeply embedded in AI-assisted creative workflows and are pushing the boundaries of what these tools can do. Editing is the core of the role, and you know how to cut short-form video that holds attention from the first frame to the last.

This is a making role. You’ll create work across formats, from short-form video and motion to design and editorial, using Runway’s products and the broader landscape of generative AI tools. Some days you’ll be cutting a launch-day Reel from generated footage. Other days you’ll be jumping on a trend the moment it breaks, building out tutorial content or exploring a creative application of a product feature no one’s tried yet. The output varies; the throughput and quality standard don’t.

Much of your work will sit at the top of the funnel, often as someone’s first encounter with Runway. It needs to stop the scroll, perform with the algorithm and feel native to each platform. You’ll also work in real time, turning model releases, trends and cultural moments into fast, reactive content while they’re still peaking.

You’ll sit within the creative department and report to the Social Media Lead. But the nature of the role means you’ll also work across product, research and marketing, often as the person who translates a product capability into a compelling creative artifact that’s geared to social audiences.

What you’ll do

  • Create high-quality short-form video, motion, design and animation for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and X using AI tools, primarily Runway’s own products

  • Edit short-form content built to hold attention, from the opening hook through the final frame

  • Develop concepts and execute finished work, not just prototypes, from initial idea through final output

  • Create top-of-funnel content that stops the scroll and performs with each platform’s algorithm

  • Respond to trends, news and cultural moments with fast, real-time content

  • Explore and push the creative boundaries of generative AI tools, finding new techniques, workflows and visual languages

  • Produce content across brand campaigns, product marketing, social, tutorials and internal demos

  • Partner with product and research teams to translate new features and model capabilities into creative work that showcases what’s possible

  • Contribute to the team’s evolving creative process by sharing workflows, techniques and best practices as the tools themselves evolve

What you’ll need

  • 4 to 8 years of professional creative experience in social, in editing, directing, design, animation, art direction, writing or a combination

  • Exceptional short-form editing skills, with a strong instinct for hooks, pacing and sound

  • A portfolio that demonstrates exceptional creative output made with AI tools, not just traditional work, and not just experimentation, but polished, intentional creative work

  • Deep, hands-on fluency with generative AI creative tools: you use them daily and understand their capabilities and constraints at a practitioner level

  • Strong visual and conceptual taste: you know what good looks like regardless of the medium or how it was made

  • Proven understanding of social media across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and X, with a strong handle on trends, formats, strategies and what each algorithm rewards

  • Real-time instincts: you spot trends early and turn quality work around fast

  • Self-direction and creative initiative: you don’t wait for a brief to start making

  • Curiosity about the technology itself: you follow model releases, experiment with new tools and understand the trajectory of generative AI

  • Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where the tools, workflows and possibilities are changing constantly

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

Working at Runway

Great things come from great teams. We’d love to hear from you.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. So regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply.
